*** THE BRENT ROLL HAS HAPPENED — THE TICKER LEVEL FALLS ~$3.70 AND IT IS NOT A PRICE FALL ***
@LCO.1 now reads "ICE Brent Crude (Dec'26)". Yesterday evening it read Nov'26 at 103.62. The front
month is now December at 99.94. So the displayed level drops from 103.62 to 99.94, about $3.68, purely
because the contract changed. CNBC has correctly rebased the comparison: @LCO.1's previous_day_closing
is 98.03, which is DECEMBER's settlement on 30 September, not November's 103.62. On a like-for-like
December basis Brent is therefore UP 1.95% (+1.91). The curve has moved up as a whole:

*** THE DAY'S SHAPE: A GLOBAL BOND ROUT, AND IT IS THE STORY ***
CNBC (approved, cached as MORN-MKT-CNBC-global-bond-rout.txt), 08:25 BST, citing LSEG:
  - US 10-year breached a level last seen in APRIL 2002, +4bp to 5.3338%
  - US 30-year +3bp to 5.6702%, its highest since JULY 2002
  - US 2-year +2bp to 4.91%
  - German 10-year bund +4bp to 3.6179%, its HIGHEST SINCE 2008
  - French 10-year +11bp to 4.9501%; Italian 10-year +10bp to 4.7171%
  - UK 10-year +5bp to 5.483%
  CNBC's stated cause: investor concern over higher interest rates, government debt loads and fiscal
  spending plans. This is what is driving the FTSE's 1.97% fall and the gilt move, so the UK number is
  not primarily a UK story today — it is the UK leg of a global repricing. Said that way in the brief.

*** GILT ADJUDICATION — CNBC's previous_day_closing REJECTED FOR THE SEVENTH TIME THIS WEEK ***
CNBC still reports the 10-year's previous close as 5.4303% — the identical value it gave at 19:08 last
night, i.e. it has not been updated for Wednesday's actual close at all. Same for the 30-year at
5.9523%. On those stale figures today's moves would be +0.048 and +0.062.
INDEPENDENT ADJUDICATOR — Trading Economics (data only), read 09:38 BST, both pages dated 1 October:
  10-year: "rose to 5.48% on October 1, 2026, marking a 0.06 percentage points increase from the
           previous session" -> implies a Wednesday close near 5.42%
  30-year: "rose to 6.02% on October 1, 2026, marking a 0.07 percentage points increase from the
           previous session"
CNBC's own article independently gives the UK 10-year as +5bp, which sits between the two.
DECISION: publish the 10-year gilt at 5.48 with a change of +0.06 on the Trading Economics basis, the
same basis used last night, which keeps the series internally consistent (5.38 -> 5.44 -> 5.48).
*** THE 30-YEAR GILT HAS GONE THROUGH 6% *** — 6.0139% on CNBC, 6.02% on Trading Economics, with an
intraday high of 6.0289%. That is the milestone worth reporting. CNBC's change_pct field for the
30-year is internally contradictory (+0.0616 points shown against -0.8617%), another reason to use the
point change and Trading Economics' framing rather than CNBC's percentage.
